title: Z-Erase: Enabling Concept Erasure in Single Stream Diffusion Transformers
claim: Prior erasure methods under-erase or produce artifacts and collapse on this architecture; ours removes concepts while preserving image quality.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right, three prompts per row, dashed divider arrow
description: A two-row image grid. The top row, labeled 'Previous Erasure' on the left, shows outputs from three baselines (AC, UCE, EraseAnything) in three columns. Each column has a large image of a person, still showing the unwanted nudity or body content with pixelation boxes, which means under-erasure. A small yellow-bordered inset holds the original output, and a small blue-bordered inset shows collapsed output such as noise, shattered textures or stripes. A dashed navy arrow with diamond ends separates the rows. The bottom row, labeled 'Z-Erase', shows three clean, high-quality results: a girl with short hair, a wheatfield with cypresses, and a selfie in an elevator. Each has a yellow inset showing the original output. Under each image is a prompt with the erased word struck through in red (naked, Van Gogh, LV). The eye goes first to the collapsed blue-box insets and then to the bottom row.
caption: We introduce Z-Erase, a concept erasure method tailored for single-stream models. First row: Prior methods adapted via our Stream Disentangled Concept Erasure Framework are tested with the "nudity" concept, showing under-erasure (AC, EraseAnything) or severe artifacts (UCE). Blue boxes reveal the generation collapse caused by naive fine-tuning without our adaptation. Second row: Z-Erase effectively removes target concepts while preserving quality. Original outputs are in yellow boxes. Sensitive content pixelated.
abstract: Concept erasure serves as a vital safety mechanism for removing unwanted concepts from text-to-image (T2I) models. While extensively studied in U-Net and dual-stream architectures (e.g., Flux), this task remains under-explored in the recent emerging paradigm of single-stream diffusion transformers (e.g., Z-Image). In this new paradigm, text and image tokens are processed as a single unified sequence via shared parameters. Consequently, directly applying prior erasure methods typically leads to generation collapse. To bridge this gap, we introduce Z-Erase, the first concept erasure method tailored for single-stream T2I models. To guarantee stable image generation, Z-Erase first proposes a Stream Disentangled Concept Erasure Framework that decouples updates and enables existing methods on single-stream models. Subsequently, within this framework, we introduce Lagrangian-Guided Adaptive Erasure Modulation, a constrained algorithm that further balances the sensitive erasure-preservation trade-off. Moreover, we provide a rigorous convergence analysis proving that Z-Erase can converge to a Pareto stationary point. Experiments demonstrate that Z-Erase successfully overcomes the generation collapse issue, achieving state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of tasks.
